title: Statins: updated adverse reaction information in patient leaflets
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 3, issue 4, November 2009
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: A European-wide review of statins reported in February 2008 identified, from clinical trial and postmarketing data, sleep disturbance, memory loss, sexual disturbances, depression and interstitial pneumopathy, and concluded that the evidence supported a possible causal relationship with statin use. Summaries of Product Characteristics and patient leaflets of simvastatin, atorvastatin, pravastatin, fluvastatin and rosuvastatin were amended: any statin may be associated with depression, sleep disturbances, memory loss and sexual dysfunction, and statins may very rarely be associated with interstitial lung disease, presenting with dyspnoea, non-productive cough and deterioration in general health such as fatigue, weight loss and fever. The review stated that the balance of risks and benefits of statins as a class remains positive.
